title: Within-game errors barely change tick to tick
headline_insight: Within an MLB game, the model's win-probability errors are almost frozen from one row to the next -- the median lag-1 residual autocorrelation is 0.9809 across 222 games.
what_it_means: Because the outcome is fixed and the probability path is smooth, consecutive in-game rows are nearly identical, so the ~78,986 in-game MLB rows carry far fewer than 78,986 independent observations. This is a guardrail about how to count evidence, not a claim about any team -- the same near-1.0 autocorrelation holds for the market path too.
how_to_read: Each game contributes one lag-1 autocorrelation of its within-game signed residual series; values near 1.0 mean rows move together, so the effective sample size is much smaller than the raw row count.
why_it_matters: It is the reason honest tests here cluster by game rather than by row -- treating every tick as independent would massively overstate confidence in any in-game finding.
caveat: descriptive_only, no edge/ROI claim; share of games with autocorrelation >= 0.9 is 0.955 for the model. Games with too few rows or flat residuals are skipped.
